_comment: Streaming dates TMDB does not know, entered by hand.
TMDB carries a digital date for a title and, measured over a full run, a
platform for four out of 142. The studio signal that was meant to cover the
gap recovered two more. So for a title like Lust Stories 3 — a Netflix
anthology whose service was public the day it was announced — there is no
automated source that knows, and the site had been printing 'Platform not
announced' about a platform that had very much been announced.
This is the answer to that, and it is deliberately small. It is not a
catalogue to keep up to date: it is for the handful of titles a month that
people are actually waiting for, where the platform is public knowledge and
no API has it yet. Everything else is left to the automated passes, and a
small regional title that nothing can place simply waits — which is the
agreed trade.
A row here is replaced by the real thing automatically. Once the title
lands, TMDB assigns a watch provider, the provider pass finds it, and the
discovered row supersedes this one. So an entry that goes stale costs
nothing; it is overtaken rather than left to rot.
Fields: title and releaseDate and platform are required. platform must be
an id from src/data/platforms.ts — netflix, prime, jiohotstar, sonyliv,
zee5, sunnxt, hoichoi, aha, lionsgate, appletv. languages are ISO codes.
kind is film or series; it defaults to film.
Only add a title whose platform you have actually seen announced. A wrong
platform is worse than no row, because it sends somebody to a subscription
they do not need — that is the whole reason the automated guess was thrown
away rather than loosened.
